objective: Curated visual sourcing for a factual NVIDIA documentary. Prefer real, scene-specific assets over generic technology stock photos.
instructions: Use visual_queries in script.json as the only primary search terms; do not concatenate full narration into image searches.
Rank returned assets by title/tag relevance. Reject low-relevance results instead of filling quotas with unrelated images.
Never use animals, shopping carts, motivational signs, unrelated transport, generic office people, books, or maps unless the narration explicitly calls for them.
For NVIDIA products, use identifiable real NVIDIA hardware or official NVIDIA newsroom media assets; do not substitute generic servers and label them as NVIDIA.
For TSMC manufacturing, label footage as illustrative unless the source confirms the specific facility or process.
Do not use AI-generated imagery as factual evidence or as a substitute for real NVIDIA products. If used for abstract transitions, label it illustrative.
Acquire only media with documented reuse terms. NVIDIA newsroom assets are leads for editorial review, not blanket proof of reuse rights; follow each asset's stated terms.

For video, prioritize official NVIDIA newsroom B-roll and clearly licensed Internet Archive footage. Do not download oversized corporate B-roll packages without selecting a relevant clip and checking its terms.
Record provider asset ID, original source page, direct media URL, creator, license, attribution, target scene and reason for selection in visual-assets.json.
Build a contact sheet and fail the render if any selected image is visibly unrelated to its scene.
